You're even dreaming in Korean? You've really improved!

usage_en: Say you prefer local hidden spots over typical tourist attractions. Just place a

examples.en: I prefer local cafés over tourist spots!
Local restaurants are tastier than tourist spots!

examples.ko: 관광지보다 로컬이 좋아, 진짜 느낌 나잖아!
examples.en: I prefer local over tourist spots — it feels more authentic!

usage_en: Describe a place as somewhere locals actually go, not a tourist trap. Just place

examples.en: This is a place where locals go!
This is a café locals go to — it's really good!

examples.ko: 현지인들이 가는 곳이야, 관광객은 잘 몰라!
examples.en: This is where locals go — tourists don't usually know about it!

usage_en: Call out a lesser-known but wonderful hidden gem of a place. Just place a noun b

examples.en: This is a hidden gem — did you know?
There's a hidden gem like this in Seoul!
It's a hidden gem — let's keep it to ourselves!

usage_en: Tell someone something is very popular and trending right now. Say what you need

examples.en: This café is really hot right now!
This drama is really hot right now — have you seen it?
It's hot right now? I should go check it out!

usage_en: Say something is totally dominating as the current mainstream trend. Say what yo

examples.en: This style is totally on trend!
This color is totally on trend these days!
It's totally on trend — try it!

usage_en: Say something or someone is currently rising in popularity. Say what you need, t

examples.en: This artist is rising in popularity these days!
This neighborhood is rising in popularity these days!
It's rising in popularity? I'm interested too!

usage_en: Say an explanation or argument makes sense to you. Say what you need, then add 말

examples.en: This logic makes sense!
What you said makes sense — you're right!
That makes sense — that should work!

usage_en: Point out that something is inconsistent or doesn't add up. Just place a noun be

examples.en: This sentence doesn't make sense.
It doesn't make sense — please explain again.
What you said doesn't make sense!

usage_en: State what happened or what will happen in the end. It works in casual and polit

examples.en: In the end, everything worked out!
In the end, I'm glad I didn't give up.
In the end, being happy is the most important thing!

usage_en: Share that something hurt your feelings or made you feel upset. Say what you nee

examples.en: I was upset — I'll be honest with you.
I was a little upset, but I'm okay now.
You were upset? I'm sorry — I didn't know.

usage_en: Express feeling wrongly blamed or treated unfairly. Say what you need, then add

examples.en: I felt wronged — thank you for understanding.
I felt wronged, but I feel better after talking about it.
That must have really felt unfair!

usage_en: Tease that a story or situation has a surprising twist ending. Say what you need

examples.en: This drama has a twist — it's shocking!
There's a twist? Don't spoil it!
There's a real twist — watch it to the end!

usage_en: Say something leaves a lingering impression long after it ends. Say what you nee

examples.en: This drama leaves a lingering impression.

examples.ko: 여운이 남아요, 한동안 못 잊을 것 같아요.
examples.en: It leaves a lingering impression — I don't think I'll forget it for a while.
It leaves a lingering impression? That's the sign of a good drama!

usage_en: Say you get totally absorbed and lost in something you're doing. Say what you ne

examples.en: This drama is totally immersive!
I got so immersed that I watched it all night!
It's a drama that really draws you in!

usage_en: Express not wanting to leave a place or moment you love. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I don't want to leave Korea — I love it so much!
I don't want to leave — I love it here so much!

examples.ko: 아직 떠나기 싫어, 더 있고 싶어!
examples.en: I still don't want to leave — I want to stay longer!

usage_en: Anticipate missing something or someone after you leave. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I think I'll miss Jisu!
I think I'll miss Korean food!

examples.ko: 한강이 그리울 것 같아, 너무 예쁘잖아!
examples.en: I think I'll miss the Han River — it's so beautiful!

usage_en: Make a firm promise to definitely come back to a place. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I'll definitely come back — I promise!
I'll definitely come back — wait for me!
I'll definitely come back to Korea!

usage_en: Mark a fluency milestone: thinking directly in Korean without translating. Just

examples.en: I think in Korean now!

examples.ko: 꿈도 한국어로 꿔요, 이제 한국어로 생각해요!
examples.en: I even dream in Korean now — I think in Korean!
You think in Korean now? That's amazing!

usage_en: Say you now understand Korean directly without needing to translate. Just place

examples.en: I understand without even translating!

examples.ko: 이제 번역 안 해도 이해돼요, 신기해요!
examples.en: I understand without translating now — it's amazing!

examples.ko: 번역 안 해도 이해돼요? 완전 늘었네요!
examples.en: You understand without translating? You've really improved!

usage_en: Note that someone's ability or skill has grown significantly. Just place a noun

examples.en: My Korean skills have improved a lot!

examples.ko: 실력이 많이 늘었어요, 포기 안 하길 잘했어요!
examples.en: My skills have improved a lot — I'm glad I didn't give up!
Your skills have improved a lot? What's the secret?

usage_en: Reflect that both of you have grown and improved through a shared journey. Say w

examples.en: I feel like we've grown together!

examples.ko: 같이 공부하면서 같이 성장한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like we grew together while studying together.
I feel like we've grown together — thank you!

literal_en: I learned so much thanks to you.
usage_en: Credit someone for helping you learn or grow a lot. Just place a noun before 덕분에

examples.en: I've learned so much thanks to you!
I've learned so much thanks to all of you!
I've learned so much thanks to you — thank you!

usage_en: Ask how long something will take — travel time, delivery, or preparation.

examples.en: How long does it take to get to Hongdae from here?
How long does delivery take?
How long does ramen take?
